content:
Facing the rapid increase in AI agents requesting "Full Disk Access" on Mac, Apple says it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

Although the company did not reveal specifics, Apple says users should understand what granting an application this kind of "extraordinary" access means.

In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that Full Disk Access in macOS was originally meant to "let backup apps function normally on Mac." However, Apple says that "some developers" are using the Full Disk Access setting in macOS in ways that "could put users at risk."

In response, Apple said it will "introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely want to give an application this kind of extraordinary access must take a very explicit action to do so."

The company did not share further details about these controls or its planned changes. It said the rise of "increasingly capable and autonomous" AI agents has made privacy and security even more important:

Apple's announcement today comes amid the growing popularity of tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots. These always-on AI agents request access to large amounts of users' personal data, and particularly with Meta Muse, we have already seen some alarming cases.
